key_insight: Online Experiential Learning (OEL) enables language models to continuously improve by extracting and consolidating knowledge from their own real-world interactions, turning deployment experience into reusable training signal.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap where deployed LLMs generate rich, useful experience but cannot leverage it for ongoing improvement because current pipelines rely on offline, human-annotated data or simulated environments.
method: Stage 1 — Experience Extraction: capture interaction trajectories (queries, responses, context, feedback) and distill transferable experiential knowledge (summaries, failure modes, corrective examples).

Stage 2 — Knowledge Accumulation & Update: store distilled experiences in a structured memory or replay buffer and use them for periodic model adaptation via retrieval-augmented prompting, selective fine-tuning, or targeted distillation.
Operational safeguards: include filtering, ranking, and privacy/safety checks to ensure high-quality, deployable experience is used for updates.
impact: OEL reduces reliance on costly human annotation and enables continuous, data-efficient improvements, yielding more robust, personalized, and up-to-date language models in real deployments.
visual_elements: Two-stage pipeline diagram (Experience Extraction → Knowledge Bank → Model Update) with arrows and short labels
Timeline/stream showing continuous interactions being converted into distilled entries stored in a knowledge repository
Before/after performance bar chart or curve comparing models without OEL vs. with OEL on real-world metrics (accuracy, user satisfaction, error rate)
Icons for safeguards: filter/shield for quality & safety, database for memory, gear for periodic model update
paper_title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
paper_authors: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Qingxiu Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang
